newsitem.title: USA: Germany's DTB launches first U.S. access point.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DTB launches first U.S. access point.

text.p: The Deutsche Terminboerse (DTB) said Thursday it launched its first U.S. access point in Chicago for trading German futures products.

DTB general manager Joerg Franke told a news briefing that two firms, Marquette Trading of Chicago and TCA of New York, had been using the Chicago site since October 21 to trade products listed on the German futures and options exchange.

Commerz Futures in Chicago, a division of Germany's Commerzbank AG, plans to begin using the DTB system in the near future and Franke said 10 firms are expected to be on the system by the end of the year.
Franke said DTB would not charge members a fee to connect to the network.
In all, DTB has 45 remote member firms that trade DTB products at the bourse's access points outside of Germany. Besides Chicago, DTB has sites in London, Paris, Amsterdam and Zurich.
DTB futures now available in the U.S. include the long-term German government bond (Bund), the medium-term German government bond (Bobl) and the DAX stock index.
Options on the futures are also available, DTB said. -Derivatives desk, 312 408-8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com
